overall: The AG found the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a meeting, crediting its denial, and declined to review the public records privilege dispute as outside OML authority.

allegations.summary: Complainant, a trustee of a realty trust, alleged the Commission deliberated outside a posted meeting about restoration plan changes reflected in a March 27 letter.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, not only does the evidence fail to show improper deliberation, it suggests that the Commission recognized the discrepancy between the March 7 vote and the March 27 letter and addressed it at its May 2 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged the AG to pierce a privilege claim the Commission raised in response to a public records request, asserting it hid off-meeting deliberations.
allegations.key_passage: We make no finding as to whether the Commission justifiably asserted the attorney-client privilege in this instance.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
